Chapter 5 of 6

The AI offer

What you will see

About 20 minutes. When a product in a shopper's cart sells out, the Online shop offers an alternative. An external AI service judges which alternative is a good substitute, but its answer counts only when it is confident enough; otherwise a safe rule decides. You put three products in one cart and sell out all three: the AI picks the offer for two of them, and the third has nothing comparable, so the AI is not even asked. The AI part is optional, so the shop still works when the AI is slow, wrong or switched off, and every offer records why it was made.

Needs: the offers layer. Lab 5.1 starts by turning it on (skip that if you chose everything at once). Lab 5.2 needs the restock layer and turns it on the same way.

Lab 5.1: Offers with a safe default #

A cart at risk is a cart item whose product's sellable stock just reached zero. Each sold-out item in a cart gets its own offer: one alternative at 10% off, a Restock notice when the product is due back soon, or both, and the shopper chooses. With neither, the shopper sees honestly that nothing comparable is in stock.

How the offer is chosen

For each cart at risk, offer-worker builds up to two eligible alternatives. With no eligible alternative there is nothing to judge, so the worker does not call Jev. Otherwise it asks Jev, an external decision API, which alternative is a good substitute, with "none of these" as an answer too. It sends each alternative compared with the sold-out product (kind, waterproofing, use, colour, price difference), the cart's value and item count, and a synthetic new-or-returning-shopper signal, never cart or shopper IDs. Jev returns a choice and a confidence score. The worker accepts the choice only if it is one of the options and its confidence is at least 0.8, the confidence threshold: then the card offers that alternative, or none. Otherwise the safe rule decides: the most comparable in-stock alternative. The Restock notice is not part of the question: it is a fact, added whenever a purchase order for the product is due within 7 days.

Note

Without a Jev key every offer comes from the safe rule with reason disabled, and LLM Observability has no AI call to show. The rest of the lab works the same way.

Open this Chapter in the demo home, group "5. The AI offer": decisions by route and reason, with links to LLM Observability and the offer-worker service.

Turn on the offers layer #

Skip this if you chose everything at once, or if offers is already in your layers: line. In demo.yaml, add offers to the line, then run:

Terminal (both paths)
make layer-on L=offers CONFIRM=yes
What this creates

This creates two Kafka topics and one more Flink statement ("cart at risk") in Confluent Cloud, starts the offer-worker Fargate service, and switches the Online shop's offer branch on. If you set jev_api_key in demo.yaml, the worker can call Jev; without it every offer comes from the safe rule.

Check with make layers-status: offers: ON. Then reload the Online shop so it shows the offer card.

1. Reset and fill the cart #

With the control panel

In the control panel, press Full demo reset on the Demo reset card and confirm. Wait for full-reset succeeded.

With the terminal

Terminal (both paths)
make reset

In the Online shop, add three products to the cart, all in EU 42: open P0042 (Trailrunner GTX) and click Add to cart, then do the same for P0048 (Dolomia Evo, Charcoal) and P0092 (Pathfinder Lite, Navy). You should see the cart badge at 3.

What adding to the cart does

The Online shop publishes one cart ADD event to Kafka per click and keeps the cart server side, so it stays after a reload. To open another product, change the product id at the end of the page address (#/product/P0048).

2. Sell out the trail shoe: the AI decides #

Go back to the P0042 product page.

With the control panel

In the control panel, on the Actions card, press P0042 next to Product ID, then Sell out product, and confirm.

With the terminal

Terminal (both paths)
make sell-out PRODUCT=P0042 GAP=1.5

You should see, a few seconds after the last store sells out, an offer card with "Decided by: AI". Either the AI chose an alternative, for example "Decided by: AI — chose Pathfinder Air (confidence 0.90, threshold 0.8)", or it judged that none is a good substitute and the card reads "Sold out everywhere. We found similar items, but none is a good match for this one." with "Decided by: AI — no good substitute". Both are correct, and the confidence changes a little from run to run.

What just happened

Flink joined your cart (topic carts.events) with the stock.sellable value of 0 and emitted a cart at risk for this cart item. offer-worker found two eligible alternatives in EU 42, the Brenta Storm (approach shoe) and the Pathfinder Air (hiking shoe), and asked Jev which is a good substitute, with their kind, waterproofing, use and price difference. Jev chose the Pathfinder Air with a confidence above 0.8, so its choice stands. If the restock layer is on, the card also shows "Back in about N hours" with Notify me above "Or switch to Pathfinder Air in Ember red, 10% off": the restock date is a fact, not part of the AI's question (Lab 5.2). The worker checked the stock again and published the offer to the offers topic, where the Online shop reads it. Alone, the safe rule would have picked the Brenta Storm, the closest in price.

The AI may also answer none (no good substitute) with a confidence above the threshold. Then no alternative is offered, and the card says that similar items exist but none is a good match, unlike the Pathfinder Lite in step 4, which has no eligible alternative at all. Earlier wording of this step: "an offer card for the Pathfinder Air that reads 'Decided by: AI — chose Pathfinder Air (confidence 0.90, threshold 0.8)'".

3. Sell out the boot: the AI picks the same boot in another colour #

Open the P0048 product page.

With the control panel

Press P0048 next to Product ID, then Sell out product, and confirm.

With the terminal

Terminal (both paths)
make sell-out PRODUCT=P0048 GAP=1.5

You should see an offer card that reads "The same Dolomia Evo in Glacier blue is in stock. Take 10% off if you switch." and "Decided by: AI — chose Dolomia Evo in Glacier blue (confidence 1.00, threshold 0.8)".

If the safe rule decides instead

The AI's choice counts only when its confidence is at least 0.8, the confidence threshold. Below it, the card reads "Decided by: safe rule" and shows the AI's suggestion with its score. The offer stays the same: the safe rule also picks the Glacier blue boot (P0059), the same kind, waterproofing and price.

4. Sell out the light hiking shoe: nothing comparable #

Open the P0092 product page.

With the control panel

Press P0092 next to Product ID, then Sell out product, and confirm.

With the terminal

Terminal (both paths)
make sell-out PRODUCT=P0092 GAP=1.5

You should see a card that reads "Sold out everywhere, and nothing comparable is in stock right now." and "Decided by: safe rule, no eligible alternative".

Why there is no offer, and no AI call

The Pathfinder Lite costs EUR 119.90. No other footwear in EU 42 is priced within 20% of it (EUR 95.92 to 143.88), so it has no eligible alternative and the worker does not call Jev: there is nothing to choose. The worker still publishes the outcome, so the shop and Datadog see the case (reason no_alternative). If the restock layer is on and a purchase order for this product is due within 7 days, the card shows a Restock notice instead: "Back in about N hours" with Notify me.

5. Open the cart #

Click the cart badge. You should see three items marked "Sold out": the trail shoe and the boot each with its offer (alternative, −10%, "Decided by: AI") and a Swap button, and the Pathfinder Lite with "No comparable product in stock".

What the cart shows, and what Swap does

The offer is the one alternative picked for that item; "AI: 0.90" next to an alternative is Jev's confidence for the option it chose. The other eligible alternative is listed at full price, the way the worker found it: same category and size, in stock now. Swap removes the sold-out item and adds the alternative through the normal cart events (ABANDON, then ADD); swapping to the offer's alternative is recorded in RUM as the action offer_accepted. When a purchase order is due within 7 days, a line "Back in about N hours" with Notify me sits under the offer line; Notify me is recorded in RUM as restock_notice_confirmed.

6. Read a Jev call in LLM Observability #

Open the LLM Observability link and open the latest trace and its offer.jev.call span. You should see in the input each alternative with its kind, waterproofing, use and price difference plus the option none, and in the output the choice and the confidence; there are two Jev calls, for the trail shoe and the boot, and none for the Pathfinder Lite.

Other ways to see this in Datadog

From the Datadog menu, the same page is AI Observability > Agent Observability > Traces, application urbanstreet-offers (the picker may show another application first). The same requests also appear in APM (service offer-worker, span offer.process); their linked logs state each decision, for example route JEV with reason accepted, or route RULE_DEFAULT with reason no_alternative for the Pathfinder Lite.

7. Use the kill switch #

In the control panel, set AI kill switch (offers_kill_switch) to 1 and press Save. Then repeat steps 1 to 4. You should see "Decided by: safe rule — AI did not return a decision" on the trail shoe and the boot (the trail shoe now gets the Brenta Storm), and the same "nothing comparable" card for the Pathfinder Lite.

More about the kill switch

This kill switch takes effect on the next offer. The reason on the dashboard is kill_switch, and the worker makes no Jev call. On the stock dashboard, in the Offers group, offer.decision by route and reason shows each of your runs.

8. Restore the defaults #

In the control panel, on the AI kill switch row, press Reset to default. You should see the value back at 0. Then reset; a reset does not change the offer settings, which is why you restore the kill switch first.

With the control panel

Press Full demo reset and confirm.

With the terminal

Terminal (both paths)
make reset

Checkpoint #

  • One cart showed three sold-out items: two offers decided by the AI and one "nothing comparable" (step 5).
  • An offer.jev.call span showed the options in its input and the choice and confidence in its output (step 6).
  • With the kill switch on, the safe rule decided every offer (step 7).

Summary

The shop does not depend on the AI. Fixed rules decide what may be offered, the safe rule always gives an answer, the AI is asked only when there is a real choice, and the trace shows why each offer was made. An offer is only an offer: nothing in this lab proves that it saved a sale.

Also in this chapter: Lab 5.2, restock that learns (optional)

Lab 5.2: Restock that learns #

About 15 minutes. When a product sells out, nobody can buy it until new stock arrives. Someone has to notice and order more, early enough and in the right amount. Here the system does it by itself: you sell out a product and watch the sale turn into restock requests, then into purchase orders, and finally into a delivery that puts the product back in stock.

A demo clock saves you from waiting days for a delivery: by default, one real minute counts as one business hour.

How Flink decides when to reorder

Flink learns two values: each store's demand rate (units sold per hour, from recent sales) and the supplier lead time (order to delivery, from past purchase orders).

Flink adds the stock on hand and the stock already on order. When that total falls to the reorder point (demand rate × lead time × safety factor), Flink emits a restock request.

Open this Chapter in the demo home, group "5. The AI offer". The restock charts themselves are in the Restock group of the stock dashboard (step 6).

Turn on the restock layer #

Skip this if you chose everything at once, or if restock is already in your layers: line. In demo.yaml, add restock to the line (for example layers: core,releases,restock), then run:

Terminal (both paths)
make layer-on L=restock CONFIRM=yes
What this starts

This starts the procurement database and the supplier simulator on the VM, registers the two procurement connectors, and creates three more Flink statements in Confluent Cloud (demand, procurement, restock) with a Datadog restock group and monitors.

Flink bills for the statements while they run; the pool stays capped at 5 CFU. The command waits for the first records before it starts the statements, so give it several minutes. Check with make layers-status: restock: ON.

1. Reset and sell out #

With the control panel

  1. In the control panel, press Full demo reset on the Demo reset card and confirm.
Why Full demo reset, not Reset demo data

When the restock layer is on, it also cancels open purchase orders and clears the restock ETA keys in Redis. Reset demo data does neither of these, so use Full demo reset.

  1. In the Online shop, open P0042 and click Add to cart.
  2. In the control panel, on the Actions card, keep P0042 in the Product ID field and press Sell out product. Wait for succeeded: Source and Redis verification completed.

With the terminal

Terminal (both paths)
make reset

In the Online shop, open P0042 and click Add to cart. Then:

Terminal (both paths)
make sell-out PRODUCT=P0042 GAP=1.5

You should see the five {"store": ..., "remaining_store": 0, ...} lines from Lab 1.1.

2. Watch the ETA appear #

Open the product page of P0042. After a few seconds it shows "Out of stock online" with "Back in stock in about N hours" and the note "demo clock: 1 min = 1 h", and the offer card shows both choices: "Back in about N hours" with Notify me, and "Or switch to" an alternative at 10% off.

More about this step

What the ETA is. This is the ETA. The default lead time is 48 business hours and each order gets a random variation (jitter), so N is a few tens of hours. We saw 28, 29 and 37.

The same due date feeds the offer card from Lab 5.1: whenever a purchase order for the product is due within 7 days, the card shows it beside the alternative, so the shopper chooses between waiting and switching. The AI is asked only which alternative is a good substitute; the date is a fact, never its choice.

What just happened: the order loop. This is the loop that just ran:

What just happened: Flink emitted one restock request per store. A JDBC sink connector wrote each request into the procurement database as a purchase order, and Debezium streamed the orders back into Kafka. That is how Flink knows the stock is on order and does not order it twice. The supplier simulator (supplier-sim) wrote the earliest due time to Redis, and the page shows it as the ETA.

3. Open the control panel #

Open the control panel in both paths and scroll below the cards to the restock settings. You should see the restock parameters: supplier lead time, lead time jitter, safety factor, coverage after delivery, minimum order quantity, demand window and the demo clock (time_compression, 60 by default).

Your changes become Datadog events

Each change you save is also sent to Datadog as an event.

4. Shorten the lead time #

Set the supplier lead time to 2 business hours, which is 2 real minutes with the default clock.

With the control panel

Set Supplier lead time (base) (lead_time_s, in business seconds) to 7200 and press Save.

With the terminal

Terminal (both paths)
make lead-time SECONDS=7200
Expected output
lead time set to 7200 s (applies to every open purchase order on supplier-sim's next cycle, every second)
More about this step

With the control panel

The change becomes a Datadog event. The panel also sends this change to Datadog as an event, which you see in step 6.

With the terminal

No event marker from the terminal. This command sends no event to Datadog, so step 6 shows no marker for it. If you want the marker, set Supplier lead time (base) to 7200 in the panel and press Save instead: a setting is not routing, so it does not mix the paths.

What happens to open orders. Every open order is rescaled and keeps its own jitter.

5. Watch the delivery #

After about a minute (the exact time depends on the product), you should see the page go back to "N available online".

How the delivery travels

After about a minute (the exact time depends on the product), the supplier calls restock() in each store's database. That is an ordinary stock update, like a sale but marked restock, so it travels the same path and the page goes back to "N available online". N depends on the demand Flink has learned and on the coverage setting.

6. See it in Datadog #

On the stock dashboard, open the Restock group. restock.orders.open rises after the sell-out and falls at delivery. Next to it are restock.orders.delivered by store and restock.lead_time.

The config-change events, and the Flink statements in Confluent Cloud

If you saved the lead-time change in the panel, it shows as an event marker on restock.orders.open and as a demo config: lead_time_s = 7200 entry in the Demo panel: config changes and actions list. That list also shows each panel action, such as a sell-out or a reset, as demo action: <name> started, then succeeded or failed. These events have the tags project:dd-demo, stack:hybrid and demo_event:config or demo_event:action, so you can also find them in the Events Explorer.

Optional: in the Confluent Cloud console, open the environment's Flink section. It lists the Flink statements dd-demo-hybrid-*. The -0 statements create the output tables. The -1 statements are the long-running inserts (sellable-1, demand-1, procurement-1, restock-1, offers-1).

Checkpoint #

  • The page shows P0042 available again (step 5).
  • Verify passes. Control panel: Verify on the Checks card shows VERIFY PASSED · Terminal: make verify prints zero mismatches (how in Lab 1.1).

Summary

The stream triggered the reorder directly, with no batch job, and you could change its parameters from the panel while it ran. The restock numbers come from a simulation. They are not a forecast.

Switch to the terminal path?

Pick one path and use it from start to finish. The control panel and the terminal each remember their own last routing for Rollback, so mixing them in one run can roll back to the wrong state. Switch only if you are starting a lab from a reset.
